events.description: Beneath the cobblestones of the Royal Mile, the cries of rebellion, sermons, and secret agreements still echo. Edinburgh stands proud, but the city hides a darker and stranger layer.

A spire pierces the Edinburgh sky, blackened by centuries of secrets and storms. The city below shudders with history both whispered and shouted. Uncover a side of Edinburgh most never see on this self-guided audio tour. Move from the looming Scott Monument to the timeworn stones of Greyfriars Kirk, through the halls of New College and beyond, chasing the tales that haunt every step. Why did a silent midnight duel near the kirk change the fate of a nation? Which monument conceals the scars of a forgotten rebellion? What odd ritual once echoed through New College's secluded courtyards? Wander ancient closes and grand crescents. Trace the city's shadows and scandals in corners tourists rush past. Every moment here tilts between awe and revelation, promising fresh eyes on a living legend. Take the first step into Edinburgh's tangled heart and let its true story unfold.

Elfman’s music blends playfulness with menace, tenderness with grandeur — a perfect mirror of Burton’s visual imagination. Alongside Elfman, highlights include unforgettable moments from Corpse Bride, the cult favourite Beetlejuice, the gothic sweep of Batman, and the razor-sharp drama of Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street. Once Upon A Leeds, 1981. The March Violets strum their first riff and scrawl their first set list. Their impressive post-punk legacy stretches from 1980s BBC John Peel Sessions, indie chart success Radiant Boys EP, Grooving in Green, Snake Dance and Turn to the Sky (featured in the John Hughes movies, Some Kind of Wonderful), all the way to the 21st century reunion, headlining festivals across Europe & the USA and storming Record Store Day 2021 with sell-out double album Big Soul Kiss. And now, for the first time The March Violets are releasing their full back catalogue, with worldwide distribution via Jungle Records. Founder-members Rosie Garland (performer, poet and author) and Tom Ashton (guitarist, producer and studio owner) are joined by William Faith (musician and vocalist with Faith & the Muse, Conflict and the Bellwether Syndicate). They are excited to be back in the studio and recording their new album set for release in the summer of 2023 and also planning live dates in support of this and their back catalogue releases. They are joined by the mighty Rose Of Avalanche, one of Leeds' finest bands and purveyors of such beauties as L.A Rain, Always There etc.

Three men, three eras and one hidden connection shape this boldly cinematic Spanish drama about love, secrets and the weight of the past. Shifting between 1932, 1937 and 2017 with ease, at first these three stories seem completely separate, but gradually connections emerge between the men at their centre. Desire, buried family truths and a forgotten piece of history bind their lives across generations, with an unfinished work of Federico García Lorca hanging over the whole story. From its virtuoso opening scene, this sweeping epic announces itself as an assured piece of filmmaking. Stunning location work, breathtaking composition and meticulous period detail create a richly textured world where personal and national histories collide. Look out for supporting turns from Glenn Close and a heavily award-tipped Penélope Cruz.

Laurie Corlett-Donald is a solo artist based in Edinburgh who makes contemporary classical music blended with electronic ambient undertones. He started his career playing in bands when he was nineteen including Discopolis and Stillhound, touring extensively and releasing three records he turned his hand to solo music production, initially releasing club music under the moniker Trembler until he shifted towards more ambient sonics and string arrangements. After many years of learning and experimenting the project turned into ‘Dunedin’ - a multimedia exploration of his hometown. Drawing on experiences of wanting to be away from Edinburgh, going out and seeing new places and yet inevitably ending up back there, the record acts as a homage to a city that is entrenched in the soul of who he is. Collaborating with local writers, short stories were made for each of the tracks that he made and the namesake comes from the stories, not the other way around. The only brief being - ‘your connection to Edinburgh’. For the live show he is going ‘off grid’ as much as possible, blending analog modular, piano and synths with Justyna Jablonksa on cello, Emma Lloyd on violin and Luisa Brown on fiddle and electronics to reimagine the album for a live environment.
